title: Fanout & fallback tool-runner with recursion throttle and transactional result anchoring
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The current executor struggles with multi-target fanout patterns when combined with tool result injection and streaming responses. In high-concurrency requests we observed runaway recursive invocations when a tool result triggers additional tool calls without a robust throttle/transaction boundary. This causes tail latency spikes and excessive token usage for some customers.

Goal: Implement a fanout-capable tool-runner that: 1) supports ordered and unordered fanout (parallel/serial), 2) provides a per-request recursion/loop throttle (configurable depth + token budget), 3) anchors tool results with transactional semantics so injected results are idempotent and safely replayable, and 4) exposes compatibility hooks for existing structured-output and function-calling APIs so we avoid breaking hosted SDK integrations.

Non-goals: Full grammar-based static analysis of tool call graphs; this ticket focuses on runtime guards and result anchoring, not a full static verifier.

Design highlights: 1) Fanout scheduler: schedule children invocations with backpressure-aware concurrency limits (default max_parallel=4, configurable per-route). 2) Recursion throttle: token-budget and invocation-depth counters attached to request context (budget consumed by generated tokens and by tool result size). When thresholds are exceeded, we short-circuit to a configurable fallback (noop result, partial aggregation, or error). 3) Transactional result anchoring: each tool invocation writes a compact result-summary into the request snapshot store (idempotent key = request_id + tool_call_signature). On replay we use the anchored result to avoid re-running expensive external tools. 4) Streaming & structured output compatibility: streamed chunks carry control frames that mark injected-result boundaries and recursion metadata so existing streaming parsers can remain compatible. 5) Backwards compatibility layer: the compatibility adapter translates old function-calling result envelopes to the new anchored format for older SDK clients.

Acceptance criteria in this ticket focus on correctness and safety: see acceptance_criteria below for specifics.
acceptance_criteria: Can execute a request that fans out to N tools with ordered reduction and return a single aggregated structured output without deadlocks or resource leaks.

Recursion throttle prevents more than configured depth (default 6) and token budget (default 2k tokens) per request; when threshold exceeded the configured fallback is used and a defensive metric is emitted.
Transactional anchoring prevents re-execution of identical tool calls across retries and replays; unit tests cover replay and dedup behavior.
Streaming responses include control frames for injected-result boundaries and are parsable by the current streaming SDKs without upgrade; integration test with python/js SDKs passes.
Compatibility adapter correctly rewrites old function-calling envelopes to anchored results for at least two major client versions (v1.3, v1.4).
E2E perf test shows no >2x increase in median latency for single-tool requests and bounded tail impact on fanout workloads compared to baseline runtime-1.21.
All new code paths are covered by unit and integration tests and documented in the runtime dev doc and the console rollout guide.

notes: Follow-up sub-issues: ENG-78103 implements the NDJSON fallback wrapper for older streaming parsers; ENG-78104 adds ops-visible metrics (recursion_throttle_hits, anchored_replays, anchored_miss_latency). Consider later a static analyzer to warn about unbounded fanout patterns in prompt templates.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (this ticket): shipping scheduler + recursion throttle + transactional anchoring and a compatibility adapter for streaming/function-calling. Phase 2 (follow-ups): NDJSON fallback, ops metrics, canary rollout via console with a 'fanout-safe' toggle. Ship into runtime-1.22 canary cluster, measure for 2 weeks, then gate into GA release.
risks_mitigation: Risk: anchor store adds latency on first-run of a tool. Mitigation: anchor writes are asynchronous with local optimistic-cache; replay path uses anchored result synchronously but fresh writes don't block the request if configured write_mode=async. Risk: compatibility adapter could break malformed older clients. Mitigation: strict validation and a safety opt-out header for bypassing rewriting.
estimated_qa_steps: Run unit tests for fanout scheduler with ordered and unordered modes.
Integration: simulate nested tool-invocations and verify throttle kicks in at configured thresholds.
Streaming integration: verify control frames parsed by python/js SDKs and legacy NDJSON fallback works.
Replay test: simulate transient worker crash and verify anchored result prevents re-run.
Perf: run fanout benchmark with 1, 4, 16 parallel children and compare median + p99 to baseline.
